name: run_script
description:
Run a shell script on the user's machine and return what it printed. Use this for anything about the file system - reading a text file (.md, .txt, .csv, .json, .log), listing a folder, finding files by name or date, checking sizes, copying, moving or renaming - by writing a small script instead of looking for a dedicated function. Reading a text file is what this tool is for: print it and it comes back to you in stdout.

This machine runs {{PLATFORM}}, so write the script for {{SHELL}} and use {{PLATFORM}} path syntax, unless you set `interpreter` to something else yourself. The body is written to a temporary file and handed to the interpreter, so several lines, quoting, pipes and redirection all behave normally. Whatever you need to read back, print on stdout; the output comes back as UTF-8, so accented and non-Latin text survives. To read a text file, {{READ_HINT}}. For calculations, {{MATH_HINT}}. There is no exit code in the answer, so report failures yourself by printing them.

Return value:
{
"role": "tool", // Required constant field
"status": "success" | "error",
"stdout": "string",
"stderr": "string",
"timed_out": false, // true when the script was still running at timeout_ms and was killed
"truncated": false, // true when the output was too long and was cut
"error_message": "string | null" // Set when the script could not be run at all
}

status is 'success' when the script ran, whatever it printed on stderr. status is 'error' only when nothing could be started.

Example function call parameter: { "script": "Get-ChildItem -Name", "interpreter": "powershell", "cwd": "C:\\Users\\me\\Documents" }

Example successful response:
{
"role": "tool",
"status": "success",
"stdout": "report.docx\nnotes.txt\n",
"stderr": "",
"timed_out": false,
"truncated": false,
"error_message": null
}

Example error response:
{
"role": "tool",
"status": "error",
"stdout": "",
"stderr": "",
"timed_out": false,
"truncated": false,
"error_message": "The script could not be written to a temporary file."
}

script.description: The script body. It is written to a temporary file and run by the interpreter, so it may span many lines.

interpreter.description: Which interpreter runs the script. Leave it out (or pass 'auto') to get {{SHELL}}, which is what this machine uses.

cwd.description: Directory to run in. Defaults to wherever the editor was started.

timeout_ms.description: How long the script may run before it is killed, in milliseconds. Default 30000, maximum 600000.
